transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Oh, hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, well, I'm mostly doing alright, really I am, but... I guess I came in because I've been having this sort of silly feeling lately, and I just wanted to make sure everything is okay. Even on my better days, I just... I can't quite shake the feeling that some of the people at church, and maybe in my walking club, are sort of keeping an eye on me? Like they're watching me. 

And sometimes it feels like they're putting little messages about me in the Sunday bulletin, or hiding them in things they say to each other. I know that probably sounds terribly strange, doesn't it? I hope it's alright that I brought that up... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel completely certain that these people are watching you and that the bulletin contains messages about you, or do you think it might only be a possibility?

Oh, goodness... I try very hard to tell myself it's just a possibility. I really do. I don't want to sound unreasonable to you, and I certainly don't want to make a fuss over nothing. 

But... well, like I was saying, even on my better days, I just can't seem to shake it. When I'm at the walking club or sitting in the pews, the feeling that they are watching me is just so strong. And the things in the bulletin, or the little comments they make to each other... it just feels very real to me, even when I try to talk myself out of it. 

I hope you don't think I'm completely losing my marbles for saying so... Does that make sense? I just want to be honest with you so I'm doing this right.
How long have you been feeling that people at church or your walking club are watching you and placing messages about you in the bulletin?

Oh, my... let me think. I suppose... well, it's probably been about eleven months now. 

I haven't really wanted to admit it to anyone, because I know how it sounds, and I certainly don't want to be a bother. But since I want to be a good patient and tell you everything... it hasn't just been the messages. For those same eleven months, I've also been... well, hearing some voices, occasionally. And just having a little trouble keeping my thoughts straight. 

It's really not too terrible, I promise, I try very hard to just push through it so it doesn't upset anyone! I hope it's alright that I'm sharing all this... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details. Am I doing okay? Is that what you needed to know?
Since these experiences began, has there been a noticeable decline in how you manage work, relationships, or everyday self-care?

Oh, well... I really try my best to keep on top of everything, I do. I still live at home, all by myself, and I manage quite a bit! But... I suppose things have slowed down just a little. 

I haven't been going to my quilting gatherings as much... or the walking club, like I mentioned. And my garden is looking a little wild these days. I just haven't had the energy for it. My daughter, bless her heart, she's so sweet... she's started popping by a bit more often to make sure I'm eating properly and getting to my appointments. 

I feel terrible being a burden to her, but she insists. I really am trying to keep up with things, though! I hope that doesn't make me sound too incapable... I just want to be honest with you. Does that answer your question alright?
Did these experiences begin after using a recreational drug or starting or changing a prescribed medication?

Oh, no, no... nothing like that. I've never touched any of those recreational drugs in my life, I promise you. I wouldn't dream of it. 

And as for my regular medications... well, my doctor for my blood pressure and cholesterol has kept me on the exact same little pills for years now. Nothing new at all. I always take them exactly as I'm told, right on schedule. 

So I don't think it could be anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information... am I being helpful?
During those eleven months, have the voices or beliefs about people watching you been present most of the time, without a symptom-free period lasting several months?

Oh, my... let's see. I really don't want to make it sound like I've been... well, completely out of sorts this whole time. 

I suppose... yes, they've been there quite a bit. But I wouldn't say every single second of every day! There are times when I'm just watching my programs and everything feels perfectly fine and quiet. I don't think there's ever been a whole month where everything just completely went away, though... maybe just a few good days here and there. 

I really do try to just focus on the positive days and not let the other times bother me too much. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining... I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for?
Have the voices or beliefs about being watched continued, at least to some degree, for six months or longer without fully disappearing?

Oh, dear... well, yes, I suppose it has been longer than six months. If I'm being perfectly honest—and I do want to be a good patient for you—it's been about eleven months now. 

The... the voices, and those messages, and just having a little trouble keeping my thoughts straight sometimes... they've been hanging around since about then. I really tried to just ignore them for the longest time, hoping they'd just fade away on their own so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it. I know eleven months sounds like a long time to let something go on, and I feel a little silly admitting it's been nearly a year. 

I hope it's alright that I tried to manage it myself for so long... I'm doing my best to explain it all properly now. Is that the timeline you were needing to know?
Have the voices or beliefs about being watched occurred during times when your mood felt normal, rather than only during a prolonged period of depression or unusually elevated mood?

Well... yes, I think so. I don't want you to think I've just been sitting around feeling sorry for myself this whole time. 

There was actually a really nice stretch... oh, maybe for a few weeks... where I was feeling quite a bit better. I was getting up and dressed every morning, eating my meals properly, and I just didn't feel quite so... heavy and weighed down, you know? I was really trying my best to be cheerful. 

But, well... even during that good patch, I was still hearing my name being called out when I was alone in the house. And... and when I went to church, I still couldn't shake the feeling that people were whispering and dropping little hints about me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit strange... I was doing so well with my mood, I just don't know why those other things didn't go away too. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
